consensus_summary: The settled primary symbol of the ship is the Church (Barque of Peter / typological Noah’s ark), the vessel that carries believers safely through the storms and sea of the world toward salvation; secondary readings include the individual faith-voyage, merchant ships as worldly commerce/pride (Tarshish, Tyre, Babylon), and occasional minor uses (Jonah’s flight, instability).
book_summary: A ship is an organized kingdom, city, or state riding on the sea of peoples, steered by its rulers and crewed by its inhabitants; Christ rules the waters without needing a vessel, yet any ship He boards is brought under its true Head.
book_core_identification: an organized kingdom/city/state on the sea of peoples
boundary_disagreement: Consensus centers the positive ecclesial/salvific vessel and treats mercantile or political ships (Tyre, Babylon, Tarshish) as secondary negative images of commerce and pride; the book reverses the priority, making political entities the core referent and thereby reclassifying or demoting the Church-as-ship reading to a mere common view.
material_contradiction: The two cores cannot both be the primary identification of the same symbol in the same sense: accepting ‘organized kingdom/city/state’ as the definition requires rejecting the consensus claim that the ship principally is the Church.
rationale: Consensus responses A–D uniformly isolate the Church (via ark typology, stilling-of-the-storm pericopes, and Barque-of-Peter tradition) as the stable primary meaning. The book explicitly flags that reading as only ‘commonly taught’ and substitutes a distinct political-polity definition whose printed citations (Ezek 27, Isa 23, Rev 18, Jonah, Acts 27) foreground Tyre/Babylon-style entities rather than the ecclesial texts. This is replacement of the central referent, not a boundary adjustment around the same core, hence DIVERGENT.
strongest_objection: One could argue the book merely broadens a latent political reading already present in the Tyre/Babylon alternatives, preserving a generic ‘vessel on the sea’ category and therefore should be scored REFINED rather than DIVERGENT.
